questions.q: What does adding a `for` expression to a Bicep resource block do?
options: Expands that single block into one resource per entry in an array, instead of writing a separate block for each
Only works inside a `module` block, never inside a plain `resource` block
Converts the resource block into a Terraform module automatically
Deletes the resource if the array is empty
questions.explain: resource storageAccts '...' = [for name in storageNames: { ... }] deploys one storage account per entry in storageNames from a single block.

questions.q: How do you deploy a Bicep resource only when a parameter is true?
options: Set the resource's `name` property to `null`
There is no way to conditionally deploy a resource in Bicep
Add `if (condition)` right after the `=` in the resource declaration
Wrap the resource in a `for` loop with one iteration
questions.explain: resource nsg '...' = if (deployNsg) { ... } deploys the resource only when deployNsg evaluates to true; otherwise it's skipped entirely.

questions.q: What is a symbolic name in Bicep, such as `storageAccts` or `nsg`?
options: The actual Azure resource name that appears in the portal
A placeholder that must match the resource group's name
A required Azure tag applied to every resource
A name chosen only for referencing that resource elsewhere in the same Bicep file; Azure itself never sees it
questions.explain: Symbolic names exist purely within the Bicep file for referencing a resource from elsewhere in that file — they are not sent to Azure Resource Manager.

questions.q: In `resource blobService '...' = { parent: storageAccts[0] ... }`, why doesn't this need an explicit `dependsOn`?
options: Child resources never have dependencies on their parent in Azure
dependsOn is only required for resources created with `for`
Bicep infers the dependency (and scope) automatically from the reference to storageAccts[0]'s symbolic name
`parent` disables dependency checking entirely
questions.explain: Referencing another resource's symbolic name — here through `parent` — lets Bicep compile the correct dependsOn and scope into the ARM JSON automatically.

questions.q: What happens to a resource guarded by `if (deployNsg)` when `deployNsg` is `false`?
options: It is never submitted to Azure Resource Manager — skipped entirely, not created and then removed
It is created and then immediately deleted by Azure
It is created but left in a disabled state
Bicep throws a compile error
questions.explain: A false `if` condition means the resource is skipped from the deployment outright; it's never created in the first place.
